name: pysystemtrade
methods: Volatility-normalised EWMAC trend: EWMA price difference using fast/slow spans divided by daily price-unit volatility
EWMAC example parameter pairs 8/32 and 16/64, with documented 16/64, 32/128, and 64/256 rule variations
Forecast scaling and clipping, with upstream example cap 21 and default cap 20
Instrument inverse-volatility weighting, correlation-aware diversification, and portfolio volatility targeting
reuseDecision: Do not reuse or port upstream code. The inspected LICENSE is GPLv3 and the project is a Python automated-futures/Interactive-Brokers engine. Implement the published EWMAC and risk method independently in TypeScript, use only Zax-approved historical data, and keep all outputs paper-only with no broker or order path.
requirements: Licensed daily historical price data with retained source/vintage; a data provider may be paid and data is not bundled with pysystemtrade
For futures: reproducible adjusted-continuous/roll policy, underlying contract data around roll dates, and multiplier/currency/FX metadata if reporting notionals
Predeclared no-look-ahead calibration windows, volatility settings, signal cap, risk target, cost assumptions, and deterministic paper-result tests
No IB account, Gateway/TWS, ib_async, MongoDB, Parquet, GitHub token, or pysystemtrade installation is required for the recommended independent implementation
If GitHub public metadata is ever read, unauthenticated REST access is 60 requests/hour per originating IP; it is unnecessary for the runtime product
